_readme: Ground truth for the eval suite. Each fixture page has one or more deliberately planted bugs. `keywords` is a list of alternatives -- a fixture's bug counts as 'found' if ANY finding on that job has tier == tier and one of these substrings (case-insensitive) in its title. This only measures recall against known-planted bugs; it does NOT auto-score precision, since that requires knowing every real bug on a page, not just the planted ones -- see agent/eval/run_eval.py's per-page 'extra findings' output for manual precision review.

planted_bugs.label: form submits with empty required field
LCP over threshold (~2.2s artificial server delay)

fixtures._note: This fixture originally relied on this deployment's own site-wide missing CSP/X-Frame-Options/X-Content-Type-Options headers as its 'planted bug' -- those were real gaps at the time. They were found and fixed in next.config.ts during a security hardening pass, which means this fixture's page now genuinely has all of them and can no longer demonstrate the bug it was designed to test. Left with zero planted bugs (rather than deleted) so the eval suite still runs a real scan against it and the history stays honest: the fixture didn't fail, the underlying gap it tested got closed. Strict-Transport-Security was never a valid expectation here either -- Vercel injects it at the edge for every HTTPS deployment regardless of app code.

planted_bugs.label: navigation link does not change URL or load new content
